title: Random-Oracle Unitary Synthesis is Impossible
authors: Andrew Huang, Akshar Ramkumar, John Wright
abstract: A major open problem in quantum complexity is the question of unitary synthesis---namely, is it possible to efficiently implement any unitary, given the ability to evaluate any classical function in superposition? Inspired by a recent work by Brakerski and Yuen (CRYPTO 2026), we propose an ``average-case'' unitary synthesis problem, which asks whether it is possible to efficiently implement a Haar random unitary given access to a random Boolean function. We then demonstrate a superpolynomial query lower bound, establishing that unitary synthesis in this model is impossible.   Along with our main result, we settle in the negative a question Brakerski and Yuen pose, of whether scalable pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) can be implemented in the ROM-PRU model. In particular, we show that in the ROM-PRU model, no $Ω(N^{1+γ})$ unitary design on $n$ qubits, where $N=2^n$, can be efficiently achieved for any $γ> 0$. On the other hand, we construct an $O(N)$-design in $\text{poly}(n)$ queries in the same model, surpassing the previously best known results which constructed $O(\sqrt{N})$-designs.
summary: This paper proves that efficiently synthesizing arbitrary random unitaries using only access to a random oracle is impossible, establishing a superpolynomial query lower bound. It also resolves a related question by showing that scalable pseudorandom unitaries cannot be implemented efficiently in the ROM. The results place strong theoretical limits on what can be computed quantumly given limited access to randomness.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental question of unitary synthesis: determining if any arbitrary unitary operation can be efficiently implemented using only access to a random classical function in superposition.
main_result: The authors prove a superpolynomial query lower bound for random-oracle unitary synthesis, establishing that it is impossible in the average-case model. They also show that scalable pseudorandom unitaries cannot be efficiently implemented beyond $O(N)$ queries.
method: The analysis involves establishing lower bounds by analyzing the required number of queries ($k$) needed to achieve a certain fidelity ($\epsilon$) in approximating the target unitary, using techniques related to quantum information theory and complexity theory.
model_or_system: The work is set in the Random Oracle Model (ROM) for quantum computation, focusing on the synthesis of Haar random unitaries. The system involves quantum circuits that query a random Boolean function $f$.
key_observables: The primary observables are the error $\epsilon$ in the synthesis approximation and the number of queries $k$ required by the algorithm.
important_parameters: The dimension $N=2^n$ (related to the Hilbert space size), the error $\epsilon$, and the query complexity $k$ are central parameters.
main_assumptions: The impossibility result holds under the assumption that the error $\epsilon$ is bounded away from 1 by a $1/	ext{poly}(n)$ factor.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the unitary synthesis problem in the ROM, then presents the main theorem establishing the superpolynomial lower bound on queries. It follows this by settling the negative question regarding scalable PRUs, providing both lower and upper bounds on the required queries.
why_interesting: This work establishes fundamental computational barriers for quantum algorithms, showing that achieving perfect randomness or universal unitary simulation requires resources (queries) that scale prohibitively with system size.
